posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Intro
During the final matches of the European Championship Football (known in America as soccer), I've been enjoying the games together with some members of the forum. During the tournament, an idea started to grow inside my brain. I wondered if it would be possible to create a football manager with RPG maker MV. I wasn't thinking about the world cup just yet, but actually about the main leagues or Europe.
But after I enjoyed the final matches of the European Championship with some friendly forum members, I got excited about the World Cup in 2024. And I thought it would be a great opportunity to create this manager that so far only existed in my head.
I got so excited, that I lost all my doubt about the possibilities and just started working on the project straight away. I realized it was going to be hard, but I have 2 years to realize this. Will I make it in time? We'll find out.
(Title screen is a placeholder made with CC0 photo. I'm open for suggestions.)
About the game
When the game starts, the plugin I wrote will generate 12 groups, each with 4 teams. This makes 48 teams, each with 24 players. This is a total of 1152 players, each with 11 stats. Which is a lot of stats. After that it generates a schedule, in which all 104 matches of the tournament are planned in advance.
(This shows all players stats of a single team. All names and stats will be different in every play-trough.)
This all happens BEFORE the game actually starts, and it is instant. The player doesn't have to wait. Instead the player sees the team-selection screen. It shows 48 flags, one for each team that is qualified for the actual real life tournament*. After the team was chosen, the player finds out in which group their team starts. It sees the opponents for the first 3 matches.
(* On request, I will add teams that didn't qualify, as alternative teams.)
(Which team comes in which group, is completely random. In real life there is a lottery, which I might simulate for the game as well.)
Each team faces all teams in their own group. Each win gives the team 3 points, and a draw will give them 1 point. The two best players in each group, go to the 16th(!) finals!
Because there are 12 groups, which means 24 numbers 1 and 2, I don't have enough teams for 16th finals. That is why of all the teams that placed 3rd, the 6 with the best results will still go to the final rounds. This gives me a total of 32 teams in the finals.
After this moment, a draw is no longer an option. Each match has a winner, or a loser. The winner goes on, and the loser goes home. In the end, there will be only one team standing, and they will be the new champion.
The player can play this whole tournament by choosing which players are in the field, what their position is, and each player can get a few individual assignments, like : "Play defensive/offensive, play friendly/aggressive" etc. Each of those settings has a positive and a negative.
(In this screen, the player can choose their formation.)
For example, there is a midfielder on the left wing. When they are set to play offensive, they will gain a little boost on their offense stats, but a little debuff on their defensive stats. And visa versa.
When the selection and formation are finalized, the match is ready to be simulated. The player will see a little animation on the field, and can read what happens on the field in a text report, which will describe in detail everything that happens on the field for 90 minutes. (Which is all skippable, for those who don't like to wait or read...)
The whole game can be played in an hour if you skip the simulations and don't care much about the selections. But when you want to read all the reports and watch all the matches of your tournament, it will take you a couple weeks. Most players will probably read the reports of their own games only. In this case the whole tournament might take a day or so, at least if you become champion.
The Plugins
A plugin that could do what I needed it to do, didn't exist yet, so I had to write it myself.
This plugin was designed to generate databases with semi-random entrees. Like it generates 1152 players with random names... Yet the team of the Netherlands, has only Dutch names and the English has no Dutch names.
It also knows that each team needs some goal keepers, some defenders, some strikers, some midfielders and some wing players. Even though their stats are random, there is a minimum to the required skills for their position. This is to prevent there is a team where the best goal keeper is terrible at goalkeeping.
It took me about 2 weeks to complete the plugin, working around the clock, but I did it! It still needs some tweaking, balancing and polishing, but it works!
I will create a second plugin, that simulates the matches and writes a report. Of course, I will write the reports, but I will only write short pieces of a report, which will be selected and used by the plugin to create a full report. The reports will include player names and the stats including the color code.
Expected release
I hope to release the game in the first half of 2026, before the real-life tournament starts. I do not yet know if the game will be a HTML game, or a download, free, or paid.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Hell, all!!
This game is go-go-going like a train!! Well... I am not anywhere near a playable anything, but the base is there:
I have written a plugin that, once the game starts, it generates 1152 players, spread over 48 teams!
I also made the plugin create a text message with the players details, per player or per team.
Here is the screen for the full team:
Here is the screen for a single player:
As I said, I have set up 48 teams!! Yeah of the teams have 24 players. I have choosen 48 semi-random countries as teams, since I don't know who's going to participate in the tournament just yet. So I just took the countries from WC'22 and then the ones from 2018, and then 2014, and then 2010... Untill I had enough countries for the 2026 championships. (For those who don't follow the sport, WC 2026 is the first time we play with 48 teams instead of 32. So just using the teams from last tournament, won't be enough.)
So, I have made the plugin generate 1152 players in 48 countries, and... They are all placeholders.
NEXT STEP:
I am now working on the draw... This ceremony will be simulated. Meaning, before you start playing, you won't know which teams will be in the same group as which other team. I thought it would be neat to use the actual draw, and set up all the groups to be exact as they are in the actual WC 2026, however... This would mean that every play-trough is going to be same, and I don't want that.
After the draw, I will make the schedule. A virtual calendar will put all matches in a certain order. First for the K.O. rounds, then for the finals. In total I would have to plan 104 matches. Which is more than any other WC in the history of Football.
AFTER THAT:
I am probably 1 or 2 weeks further before that is all done. And it won't be until then, that I can finally start creating the game-play. I will have to make it possible for the player to:
Make a selection for the next match. (Which player starts where)
See an overview of their own and the other teams
See an overview of their own and the other group
See an overview of their own and the other matches
Set up other settings.
I will also have to create a certain AI that will set up the selection and other options for the other 47 teams.
FINAL STEP:
And only when all that has been completed, I can actually start making the simulator, which will simulate the matches and provides a report of the matches too.
So... You might think the final step means I will be done and the game can be released... But after creating the simulation, I will have to test, and to test again, and to test again, and again. In between testing, I will have to adjust formula's, stats and settings, before I test again.
And even when all that is finished, there is still more to be done. I need to create team shirts, and player faces (although, I am not going to make 1152 faces, I will randomize those too. But I will try to make European and North American teams have more white people, Asian teams more Asian people, African teams more dark people, South American more Latino people and finally Middle Eastern teams more Arabic people.)
Why randomize at all?
Good question... When I make teams from all over the works, they all need have their own shirt, they all have a default race, their names are in their own languages etc etc etc. Is it still useful to randomize those things?
Well, yes... This way, I might have to make about 50 Dutch names, and they are only used in a few countries. But when I have a list of 50 English names, which are randomly combined with 1, 2 or 3 initials for first-names, they make hundreds of random English names, which I can use for many countries.
The same goes for faces. I might have to make 50 white faces, 50 Asian faces, 50 Arabic faces and 50 black faces, but those 50 faces, I can re-use again and again, with a different shirt and a different flag (flags will be shown behind the player)
See, the faces are actually the same, but one is for the Dutch team, one for the Italian team and the last is from the English team.
So, the conclusion of this whole chapter? I have a so much work done already, but there is a lot (and when I say a lot, I actually mean a loooooooooooooooot) more to do.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Hey all!
I've been doing so much on the game. I already had 1152 players which get randomly generated at the start of the game, which is 48 teams of 24 players each.
Now I've simulated the "draw", which is a lottery kind-of event, that decides who will be placed in which group, before the final round start. All 48 teams will be randomly spread over 12 groups.
It took me a while to figure out how to make the table with the current score be sorted, so the #1 team shows on top of the list, but after lots of trial and error, I figured it out.
I was quite quick to find
array.sort((a, b) => a.points - b.points)
but for some reason, this caused errors and crashed the game. I'm still figuring out why that was, but even though the cause is unknown to me, I was able to solve the problem.
Please don't pay attention to the graphics. I didn't pay any attention to the graphics at all so far. I mainly just create those tables and windows with information, just to see if everything works.
The next thing I got to break my brain over, is to make the paying scedule. First, all teams have to face each team in their group, which results in 6 matches per group. If we call all 4 teams in the groups A, B, C and D, each group will have the following matches:
A vs B
A vs C
A vs D
B vs C
B vs D
C vs D
Now everyone in the group has played against everyone else in the group. We do this for all 12 groups, leaving us with 12x6 = 72 matches. Those will all be planned before the first game even starts.
After all those 72 matches have been played, we know who go to the finals. Planning those would need a whole different set of conditions and formula's.
All with all, this project goes as a train! I know, I am not nearly as far as I should be before I can show anything concrete, but I already have so much more done than I would ever have expected in such a short time.

Hey all!
I have news flash! Although, I already told about this in my status updates a little, so you might a a little af what I want to show you.
The original idea was to make a game for the world-cup 2026. And secretly, in the background, I wanted to work on a full version that follows full seasons of clubs in different leagues. I looked it this version as the full game, and the world cup as an event game.
The season game would have more matches, more teams and way more features. You'd manage the clubs money, their staining schedule, and even the growth of your field.
One source of income for the club, is a sponsorship. The better your club performs, the better the sponsor deals will be. Fun fact!
Some of the sponsor signs found on the sideline of the field, are actual ads for RPG maker games, made by members of this forum
.
Another source of income, is the sale of tickets. You only sell tickets for home-games. (The games where the opponent comes to your club to play).
If you finish first in the lowest league, you will be promoted to the next league. The clubs here are more advanced and have better players. You need to train your players, or buy new talents on the transfer market, to keep up with the clubs of this league.
So basically it would be a whole new game, with way more to do than in the tournament. There is no leveling your players in the world cup. There will only be 8 matches to be played, assuming you make it to the half-finals at least.
However, it makes way more sense now to work on the full game, just to strip out all unwanted features for the world cup. Working on both games simultaneously is confusing as... you know what. So I'm not going to do that. So instead of creating the World Cup first and the full game in secret, I will focus on the full game, and strip down everything later for the tournament.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
I made a training system for the game. The manager will choose one of several trainings, which can be divided in 3 groups: Focused training, Divided and Special.
Every player that participated in a match gains XP for the stats linked to the position they play on. How much XP they gain for that stats, depend on which training is chosen and how much experience they already have.
When the manager chooses a focused training, like Goalie, or Wing Defender, only those who play on the trained position will gain full experience. This can be: Goalie, Wing Defender, Center Defender, Wing Midfield, Center Midfield, Wing Offender, Striker. They will level up fast, but you can only train so many players at the same time. (Green Table)
When the manager chooses a divided training, like Defense, or Wings, at the right column or row will receive training, but they gain only 70%. This ban be: Defense, Midfield, Offense, Wings, Center.  (Yellow Table)
When the manager chooses a special training, all players on the field will gain special training, which could be Penalties, Corner, Header, Agility, Endurance. Like the divided training, special training only gains 70%, but it trains all the players. (Also Yellow Table)
Every player on the field that doesn't play on a training positions when focused or divided training is chosen, only gains 10% training. (Red Table)
The closer the players level comes to the max level (22) the less experience they gain.
With training, even the worst players can become stars, but don't forget: Your players get older as well. And you can only train 1 stat at the time. Although, even when not playing on a training position, players who just play enough matches, can still level the skills from absolute 0 to something acceptable. They will be old by the time they reach their level, but still, it will show progress in your players even when not playing on a playing position.
(Keep in mind that most players will play on a position matching their best stats, so a training will pretty much never start with level 0.)
So, that is something new, something the seasons will enjoy while it won't be included in the world cup 2026 version.
I hope the tables give a clear overview of how leveling works in the game, but if not, please ask.

Yeah? I have more experience with hattrick, which is a manager but MMO (I think you'd like it) and then when I didn't have a player to go on a certain spot, I just put in an extra player in another spot. Have 3 defenders, but only one on the left wing, have four midfielders, but again only one on the wing, on the other side. Or all 4 in the center. Just play without wings at all.
Or a 6-0-4 formation, which makes no sense at all.
But to be fair, the purpose of that wasn't to win the match, but to have players play on certain positions, to gain experience for those positions. However, I still won some matches that way. Most likely when the opponent was doing the same thing. Or the opponent might have been playing with their B-team (if they have 22+ players) to train their lesser players.
And you know what? I hope people will play my game that way too. Sacrifice a full season to train your talents (young players with promising stats), before going for the championship, or focus fully on money by buying young talents at 16/17 and train them for 3 seasons, then sell them at 19/20 for ten times the money. That last one is a waste of time, but I can't deny I did this too.
And in hattrick, a season of 12 weeks, actually lasted 12 weeks. So straining players for 3 seasons, that took about 9 months.
I admit it, I'm a nerd. But like I said, a waste of time. Going for the championship is way more fun, and gives better results, which automatically translates to more money. Specially if you become champion and get promoted to the next league.
In my game a season would be 24 weeks, but can be played in about an hour if you use the same setup and don't care for the stats or goals or anything. So spending 3 hours to sacrifice 3 seasons to tenfold the money you've invested in 4 or 5 players, might make the difference for the next seasons. Because when you sell those talents, who are now stars, you have suddenly a lot of money, which can be invested in your arena, and a few new players to train. (That is always a tough moment, though. You'll lose 5 great players! But that is what you trained them for...)
Okay, this reply is getting way too long. Besides, I'm talking about hattrick more than my own game )(Which totally got my motivated to work on my game, btw. I wrote this whole reply except for this paragraph hours ago. I just never hit the post button.)
Anyhow, I have a lot to show for soon. Maybe tomorrow, if I can find the time.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
So, I made great progress over the last few days. Before I've spend so much time making the interface in MV, I didn't actually start making the simulation for the match.
I've been working on it for days, and have a huge database of commentary line that will all me merched together in a single report for your match, all based on the stats and positions of the players.
I also created the scedule for all 5 leagues, and a function to place choose the strongest selection for all AI teams. Based on the same score that is used by the player when they set up their selection.
I did a clean remake just for the sake of refreshing my memory (even though most was just copy pasting line-for-line from one file to the other) and to put in action what I've learned since I touched this plugin last.
I did however split the plugin up into 2 plugins:
One that creates the database and creates the text output for RPG maker, and one that simulates the game.
The reason for this is simple: The database for this single plugin command and the plugin command itself, are over 2000 lines together. That is more than the rest of the entire plugin, and all the info it needs is stored in game variables.
I didn't create any interfaces with the new remake plugin yet, though. I focused on creating the plugin first. (I thought that is where I went wrong the first time...)
I am all in at this project again and I am as excited as I was the first time. Hopefully soon I have screenshots to share.
